r: Label names hardware recording with performance results; rewrite adds reproducibility.

st: Non-destructive editing must always preserve the original media file; edits are stored as revisioned recipes and exported copies only.
ac: Given an original asset, when any edit or export runs, then the original file hash remains unchanged.
r: Label names original preservation; rewrite adds the no-overwrite invariant.
vm: Non-destructive editing fixture with hash checks.

st: When the user applies a crop, Lamha must store a revisioned non-destructive crop recipe, show a preview, and never overwrite the original media.
ac: Given an asset, when a crop is applied, then the recipe is revisioned and the original file remains unchanged.
r: Label names crop; rewrite adds recipe storage and no-overwrite.

st: When the user applies a rotation, Lamha must store a revisioned non-destructive rotation recipe, show a preview, and never overwrite the original media.
ac: Given an asset, when a rotation is applied, then the recipe is revisioned and the original file remains unchanged.
r: Label names rotation; rewrite adds recipe storage and no-overwrite.

st: When the user exports an edited copy, Lamha must produce a new file from the revisioned recipe while leaving the original media unchanged.
ac: Given a revisioned recipe, when export runs, then a new edited copy is produced and the original remains unchanged.
r: Label names edited export; rewrite adds copy production and no-overwrite.

st: When AI resource use is measured, Lamha must record CPU, RAM, GPU memory, and disk usage for each worker task and report results with the hardware profile.
ac: Given a worker task, when resource measurement runs, then CPU, RAM, GPU memory, and disk usage are recorded with the hardware profile.
r: Label names AI resource use; rewrite adds measurable metrics and recording.

st: When third-party models are considered for bundling, Lamha must record licence, attribution, and redistribution review and block release if any model is unresolved.
ac: Given a third-party model, when compliance review runs, then licence, attribution, and redistribution status are recorded and unresolved status blocks release.
r: Label names third-party models; rewrite adds licence review and release blocking.

st: Sidecar separation must keep authoritative user knowledge in versioned files separate from rebuildable SQLite indexes and caches.
ac: Given an asset with sidecars and SQLite indexes, when authority validation runs, then user knowledge remains in versioned files and indexes rebuild from them.
r: Label names sidecar separation; rewrite adds the authority-separation result.

st: When a cross-drive operation is interrupted, Lamha must mark the transaction interrupted, retain source and destination bundles, and offer deterministic resume or rollback.
ac: Given an interrupted cross-drive operation, when recovery runs, then the transaction is marked interrupted and deterministic resume or rollback is offered.
r: Label names cross-drive interruption; rewrite adds manifest state and recovery.

st: When an external drive is registered, Lamha must record a durable drive identity and use it to keep detached state, pending overlays, and reconnection consistent.
ac: Given a registered external drive, when it disconnects and reconnects, then the durable identity matches and detached state and overlays remain consistent.
r: Label names external-drive identity; rewrite adds durable identity and consistency.

st: Cross-platform path handling must use the reviewed safe path rules for case, Unicode normalization, and reserved names on every supported platform.
ac: Given the same logical path on each platform, when path handling runs, then the safe name rules apply consistently and collisions are reported.
r: Label names cross-platform paths; rewrite adds platform-consistent handling.

st: When metadata corruption is detected, Lamha must preserve the corrupted bytes, mark the record degraded, and offer verified restore or manual repair without guessing fields.
ac: Given corrupted metadata, when validation fails, then the bytes are preserved, the record is marked degraded, and restore or manual repair is offered.
r: Label names metadata corruption; rewrite adds preservation and repair results.

st: When JSON and XMP conflict, Lamha must preserve both values with their sources and require an explicit review decision before one becomes authoritative.
ac: Given conflicting JSON and XMP values, when a conflict is detected, then both values and sources are retained until a decision.
r: Label names JSON/XMP conflict; rewrite adds value and source preservation.

st: When a face misclassification is detected or reported, Lamha must create a review item with the candidate, evidence, and affected person and keep the authoritative assignment unchanged until a decision.
ac: Given a misclassified face, when the misclassification is reviewed, then a review item records the evidence and the authoritative assignment remains unchanged until a decision.
r: Label names face misclassification; rewrite adds review-item creation and no-mutation.

st: When models are considered for bundling, Lamha must maintain a model inventory with licence, attribution, redistribution, and provenance review and block release while any model is unresolved.
ac: Given each bundled model, when compliance validation runs, then licence, attribution, redistribution, and provenance are recorded and unresolved models block release.
r: Legal-label under the rebranding method; rewrite replaces worker-inference wording with licence inventory and release blocking.

st: The packaged application must use the reviewed Lamha name consistently on every user-visible surface and the release gate must fail if any surface disagrees.
ac: Given the release build, when surface-name validation runs, then every surface shows the reviewed name or the release gate fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds the consistency check and failure result.

st: The packaged application must include the reviewed logo assets and display them consistently; missing or mismatched logo files must block release.
ac: Given the release build, when logo validation runs, then the reviewed logos are present and displayed consistently or release fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds presence and consistency checks.

st: The packaged application must include the reviewed icon set and use it across shell, installer, and about surfaces; missing icons must block release.
ac: Given the release build, when icon validation runs, then the reviewed icon set is present on every required surface or release fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds presence and consistency checks.

st: Package identifiers must use the reviewed Lamha identifiers and the release gate must fail if any package ID disagrees.
ac: Given the release build, when package-ID validation runs, then every package identifier matches the reviewed value or release fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds identifier validation.

st: Executable names must use the reviewed Lamha names and the release gate must fail if any binary name disagrees.
ac: Given the release build, when executable-name validation runs, then every binary name matches the reviewed value or release fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds name validation.

st: Application-data directory names must use the reviewed Lamha names and the release gate must fail if any data path disagrees.
ac: Given the release build, when app-data name validation runs, then every data directory matches the reviewed value or release fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds name validation.

st: The About screen must display the reviewed application name, version, and attribution and the release gate must fail if the About surface disagrees.
ac: Given the release build, when the About screen is inspected, then name, version, and attribution match the reviewed values or release fails.
r: Rebranding-surface label; rewrite adds content validation.

st: The release bundle must include the reviewed licence files and the release gate must fail when any required licence file is missing or unresolved.
ac: Given the release manifest, when licence-file validation runs, then every required licence file is present with reviewed evidence or release fails.
r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds presence and evidence checks.

st: Bundled binaries must carry the reviewed attribution and licence notices and the release gate must fail when any binary notice is missing.
ac: Given the release manifest, when binary-attribution validation runs, then every bundled binary has its notice or release fails.
r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds attribution validation.

st: Fonts referenced by the project must carry reviewed licence and attribution records and the release gate must fail when any font is unresolved.
ac: Given the release manifest, when font-licence validation runs, then every referenced font has a reviewed licence record or release fails.
r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds licence validation.

st: Third-party assets in the product must be inventoried with licence, attribution, and redistribution review and the release gate must fail while any is unresolved.
ac: Given the third-party asset inventory, when compliance validation runs, then every asset has reviewed licence and attribution or release fails.
r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds inventory and release blocking.

st: The release bundle must include the required copyright notices for all bundled and referenced material and must block release when any required notice is missing.
ac: Given the release manifest, when copyright validation runs, then every required notice is present or release fails.
r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds completeness and release blocking.

st: Rebranding and packaging must never remove legally required material; any removal of a licence, notice, or attribution surface must fail the release gate.
ac: Given the pre-release surface set, when the release gate runs, then no legally required material is missing or release fails.
r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds the removal prohibition and gate.

st: Review queues include the reviewed queue types (pending, deferred, suppressed, history) shown in the Review Centre.
r: Review-centre heading; reclassified as glossary.

st: Review actions include the reviewed decision set (approve, reject, suppress, defer, skip, mark intentional, apply to selection).
r: Review-centre heading; reclassified as glossary.

st: When a reviewer reviews items one by one, Lamha must present one item at a time and record each decision before advancing.
ac: Given a queue, when one-by-one review runs, then one item is presented at a time and each decision is recorded before advancing.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds sequencing and decision recording.

st: When a reviewer approves an item, Lamha must commit the approved transition with provenance and revision and leave other items unchanged.
ac: Given a pending item, when approval is confirmed, then that item commits with provenance and other items remain unchanged.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds commit scope and provenance.

st: When a reviewer suppresses an item, Lamha must persist the suppression and exclude the item and matching future items from review queues.
ac: Given a pending item, when suppression is confirmed, then the item is suppressed and matching future items are excluded.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds persistence and future exclusion.

st: When a reviewer defers an item, Lamha must persist the deferred state and restore the item to the queue unchanged on reopen.
ac: Given a pending item, when deferral is confirmed, then the item is deferred and reopen restores it unchanged.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds defer/reopen state preservation.

st: When a reviewer skips an item, Lamha must move to the next item without changing the skipped item's state.
ac: Given a queue, when skip is chosen, then the next item is presented and the skipped item's state remains unchanged.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds the no-mutation result.

st: When a reviewer marks an item intentional, Lamha must persist the intentional marker with provenance and exclude the item from future duplicate or suggestion queues.
ac: Given a review item, when it is marked intentional, then the marker is persisted and the item is excluded from matching future queues.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds persistence and exclusion.

st: When a reviewer applies a decision to a selection, Lamha must commit the decision to exactly the selected items and report per-item results.
ac: Given a selected set, when the decision is applied, then exactly the selected items change and each result is reported.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds exact scope and reporting.

st: When a reviewer asks for the suggestion reason, Lamha must display the model, source, and configuration provenance behind the suggestion without changing its state.
ac: Given a suggestion, when its reason is requested, then model, source, and configuration provenance are displayed and no state change occurs.
r: Review-action label; rewrite adds provenance display and no-mutation.

st: When an asset is opened from a review item, Lamha must load the asset for display and must not change review or authoritative state.
ac: Given a review item, when its asset is opened, then the asset displays and no review or authoritative change occurs.
r: Label names open-asset; rewrite separates navigation from mutation.

st: When Open event is invoked, Lamha must load and display the reviewed event record, members, and folders; it must not create or update an event plan merely because the event was opened.
ac: Given an event, when Open event runs, then the event data loads for display and no plan or filesystem change occurs.
r: Open-event label; rewrite separates navigation from event-plan mutation.

st: When Open folder is invoked, Lamha must open the folder in the UI or reveal its path in the OS file manager as the action requires; it must not authorize roots or mutate folder state.
ac: Given a folder, when Open folder runs, then the folder is opened or revealed and no authorization or filesystem change occurs.
r: Open-folder label; rewrite separates UI opening and OS reveal from root authorization.

st: When Open person is invoked, Lamha must load and display the reviewed person profile, faces, and links; it must not mutate person identity or assignments merely because the profile was opened.
ac: Given a person, when Open person runs, then the profile and links load for display and no identity or assignment change occurs.
r: Open-person label; rewrite separates navigation from identity mutation.

st: When a reviewer filters review items by confidence, Lamha must show exactly the items whose recorded confidence matches the filter.
ac: Given review items with confidence values, when the filter is applied, then only matching items are shown.
r: Filter label; rewrite adds the observable filter result.

st: When a reviewer filters review items by source, Lamha must show exactly the items whose recorded source matches the filter.
ac: Given review items with source records, when the filter is applied, then only matching items are shown.
r: Filter label; rewrite adds the observable filter result.
Statement is already record-specific (completion tracker preserves requirement/package status changes, rejects divergence); it does not reproduce a legacy template.

st: When a file or folder operation would collide, Lamha must detect the collision, preview the conflict, and apply nothing until the user approves a safe resolution.
ac: Given a colliding operation, when the collision is detected, then the conflict is previewed and no change occurs until approval.
r: Label names collision detection; rewrite adds detection, preview, and approval.

st: Before any file or folder mutation commits, Lamha must show a preview of the planned changes and require explicit approval.
ac: Given a planned mutation, when preview runs, then the changes are shown and commit requires approval.
r: Label names preview; rewrite adds preview and approval.

st: When a move or rename commits, Lamha must verify source and destination hashes and leave a typed error with unchanged paths if verification fails.
ac: Given a planned move or rename, when commit runs, then hashes verify at both ends and failure leaves paths unchanged.
r: Label names hash verification; rewrite adds verification and failure preservation.

st: When a sidecar is repaired, Lamha must preserve the original bytes until a validated replacement is committed and must record the repair in history.
ac: Given a malformed sidecar, when repair commits, then the validated replacement is stored, the original is preserved until commit, and the repair is recorded.
r: Label names sidecar repair; rewrite adds preservation and history.

st: When an asset bundle is renamed, Lamha must rename the media and companion sidecars together, preserve the original filename, and verify hashes before commit.
ac: Given an asset bundle, when rename commits, then all bundle members are renamed together with original name preserved and hashes verified.
r: Label names bundle rename; rewrite adds bundle cohesion and preservation.

st: When an asset bundle is moved, Lamha must move the media and companion sidecars together and verify hashes before commit.
ac: Given an asset bundle, when move commits, then all bundle members move together with hashes verified.
r: Label names bundle move; rewrite adds bundle cohesion and verification.

st: When the user restores an original filename, Lamha must rename the asset back to its preserved original name and record the restoration in history.
ac: Given a renamed asset, when original-filename restore is confirmed, then the asset returns to its preserved name and the restoration is recorded.
r: Label names original-filename restore; rewrite adds the restore result.

st: When an event folder is renamed, Lamha must rename the folder and its managed records together, preserve the original name in history, and verify hashes before commit.
ac: Given an event folder, when rename commits, then the folder and records are renamed together with original name preserved.
r: Label names event-folder rename; rewrite adds cohesion and provenance.

st: When an event folder is moved, Lamha must move the folder and its managed records together and verify hashes before commit.
ac: Given an event folder, when move commits, then the folder and records move together with hashes verified.
r: Label names event-folder move; rewrite adds cohesion and verification.

st: When an event is split, Lamha must preview the resulting events and membership and commit only after explicit confirmation while preserving historical membership.
ac: Given an event, when a split is confirmed, then the resulting events are created with membership preserved and history intact.
r: Label names event split; rewrite adds preview, confirmation, and history preservation.

st: When folders are merged, Lamha must preview the merged membership and commit only after approval while preserving every asset identity and hash.
ac: Given approved folder merges, when commit runs, then the folders merge with all asset identities and hashes preserved.
r: Label names folder merge; rewrite adds preview, approval, and preservation.

st: When folders are linked, Lamha must record the link without moving or renaming the linked folder contents.
ac: Given existing folders, when linking is confirmed, then the link is recorded and folder paths and contents remain unchanged.
r: Label names folder linking; rewrite separates linking from mutation.

st: When folder-map materialization runs, Lamha must preview the folders to create and commit only after approval while preserving existing paths.
ac: Given a folder-map plan, when materialization is confirmed, then the planned folders are created and existing paths remain unchanged.
r: Label names folder-map materialization; rewrite adds preview and approval.

st: Cross-drive file operations must use copy, flush, checksum verification, and a journaled source-removal step and must never assume that rename is atomic across drives.
ac: Given a cross-drive operation, when it runs, then copy, flush, checksum, and journaled source removal complete or the prior state is restored.
r: Label names cross-drive support; rewrite adds the non-atomic rename rule and verification.

st: When manual filesystem changes are detected, Lamha must reconcile the derived index against the current filesystem and report mismatches without altering source files.
ac: Given manual changes, when reconciliation runs, then the index updates to match the filesystem and source files remain unchanged.
r: Label names manual change detection; rewrite adds reconciliation and no-mutation.

st: When Show in folder is invoked, Lamha must reveal the asset's physical path in the OS file manager without moving files or changing state.
ac: Given an asset, when Show in folder runs, then the OS reveals the path and no filesystem or state change occurs.
r: Label names show-in-folder; rewrite adds the navigation-only result.

st: When consistency detection compares the recorded hash with the current hash, Lamha must report matches and mismatches and never overwrite or delete the file on mismatch.
ac: Given an asset, when hash comparison runs, then the result is reported and mismatched files remain unchanged.
r: Label names hash comparison; rewrite adds reporting and preservation.

st: When an orphan sidecar is found, Lamha must create a review item with the sidecar and suspected asset without deleting or modifying the sidecar.
ac: Given an orphan sidecar, when consistency detection runs, then a review item is created and the sidecar remains unchanged.
r: Label names orphan sidecars; rewrite adds review creation and no-mutation.

st: When consistency detection compares the event date with the asset date, Lamha must report the mismatch and keep both records unchanged until a review decision.
ac: Given a date mismatch, when consistency detection runs, then the mismatch is reported and no record changes until a decision.
r: Label names date comparison; rewrite adds reporting and preservation.

st: When consistency detection compares the sidecar filename with the media filename, Lamha must report the mismatch and keep the files unchanged until a review decision.
ac: Given a sidecar/media name mismatch, when consistency detection runs, then the mismatch is reported and the files remain unchanged.
r: Label names filename comparison; rewrite adds reporting and preservation.

st: When a duplicate asset ID is detected, Lamha must create a review item with both records and must not merge or delete either record automatically.
ac: Given duplicate asset IDs, when consistency detection runs, then a review item is created and neither record changes.
r: Label names duplicate IDs; rewrite adds review creation and no-mutation.

st: When consistency detection compares the event folder with the event node, Lamha must report the mismatch and keep the folder and node unchanged until a review decision.
ac: Given a folder/node mismatch, when consistency detection runs, then the mismatch is reported and nothing changes until a decision.
r: Label names folder/node comparison; rewrite adds reporting and preservation.

st: When consistency detection compares the folder year with the normalized date, Lamha must report the mismatch and keep the folder and record unchanged until a review decision.
ac: Given a year/date mismatch, when consistency detection runs, then the mismatch is reported and nothing changes until a decision.
r: Label names year/date comparison; rewrite adds reporting and preservation.

st: When JSON and XMP disagree, consistency detection must report the conflict with both values and sources and change nothing until a review decision.
ac: Given a JSON/XMP conflict, when consistency detection runs, then the conflict is reported and both files remain unchanged.
r: Label names JSON/XMP comparison; rewrite adds conflict reporting and preservation.

st: When JSON and embedded metadata disagree, consistency detection must report the conflict with both values and sources and change nothing until a review decision.
ac: Given a JSON/embedded conflict, when consistency detection runs, then the conflict is reported and both records remain unchanged.
r: Label names JSON/embedded comparison; rewrite adds conflict reporting and preservation.

st: When a required JSON sidecar is missing, Lamha must mark the asset degraded and create a review item without fabricating values.
ac: Given a missing JSON sidecar, when consistency detection runs, then the asset is marked degraded and a review item is created.
r: Label names missing JSON; rewrite adds degraded state and review.

st: When a required XMP sidecar is missing, Lamha must mark the asset degraded and create a review item without fabricating values.
ac: Given a missing XMP sidecar, when consistency detection runs, then the asset is marked degraded and a review item is created.
r: Label names missing XMP; rewrite adds degraded state and review.

st: Planning handoff must record the recommended first implementation phase for each package and must reject packages without a recommended phase.
r: Handoff field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Handoff validation must reject packages without a recommended phase.

st: Planning handoff must list the exact files required for the recommended first phase and must reject handoff without those file references.
r: Handoff field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Handoff validation must reject missing file lists.

st: Planning handoff must record code that must remain temporarily and the reviewed phase when it may be removed.
r: Handoff field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Handoff validation must require removal-phase records.

st: Mapping coverage must be measured against the reviewed source rows and must fail validation when coverage is incomplete.
r: Handoff field label; reclassified as a coverage constraint.
vm: Coverage validation must reject unmapped source rows.

st: The physical library must use normalized managed Event Folders with the reviewed naming rules and must not create folders outside the approved layout.
ac: Given a physical library, when event folders are created, then they follow the normalized managed naming rules.
r: Label names normalized event folders; rewrite adds the layout rule.

st: Manage Later intake must place newly discovered assets into the reviewed intake state without moving media until an approved operation plan exists.
ac: Given newly discovered assets, when intake runs, then they enter Manage Later state and no media moves until an approved plan.
r: Label names Manage Later intake; rewrite adds intake state and plan gating.

st: Linked Folders must be indexed in place and must never be moved or renamed by automated organization.
ac: Given a Linked Folder, when indexing runs, then its assets are indexed at their existing paths and no move or rename occurs.
r: Label names linked-folder indexing; rewrite adds in-place indexing and no-mutation.

st: The planning stage must inventory the whole codebase before mapping and must reject mapping claims for uninventoried code.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Mapping validation must require full inventory.

st: The planning stage must classify every code area and must reject unclassified areas before implementation.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Plan validation must reject unclassified areas.

st: The planning stage must double-check coverage and must not declare mapping complete while coverage gaps remain.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a coverage constraint.
vm: Coverage double-check must fail on gaps.

st: The planning stage must not delete code; all existing code remains in place until a reviewed removal plan exists.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a no-deletion constraint.
vm: Planning validation must fail on any deletion instruction.

st: The planning stage must not rename packages; package renames require a reviewed migration plan.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a no-rename constraint.
vm: Planning validation must fail on package-rename instructions.

st: The planning stage must not remove dependencies; dependency removal requires a reviewed replacement plan.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a no-removal constraint.
vm: Planning validation must fail on dependency-removal instructions.

st: The planning stage must not migrate data; data migration requires a separately reviewed implementation phase.
r: Planning-stage label; reclassified as a no-migration constraint.
vm: Planning validation must fail on data-migration instructions.

st: Event folder naming must use the approved event start date and must never derive the authoritative date from capture-time suggestions.
ac: Given an approved start date, when the event folder is named, then the folder uses that date and capture-time suggestions remain non-authoritative.
r: Label names start-date usage; rewrite adds date authority and no-inference.
Statement is already record-specific and observable (privacy removal targets GPS metadata, creates a reviewed mutation plan, preserves originals); it does not reproduce a legacy template.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets device serial data, Lamha must remove it from the exported copy while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a privacy export targeting device serial data, when the export runs, then the field is absent from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds removal and preservation results.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets identifying camera fields, Lamha must remove them from the exported copy while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a privacy export targeting identifying camera fields, when the export runs, then those fields are absent from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds removal and preservation results.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets author or creator fields, Lamha must remove them from the exported copy while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a privacy export targeting author/creator fields, when the export runs, then those fields are absent from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds removal and preservation results.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets comments, Lamha must remove them from the exported copy while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a privacy export targeting comments, when the export runs, then comments are absent from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds removal and preservation results.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets descriptions, Lamha must remove them from the exported copy while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a privacy export targeting descriptions, when the export runs, then descriptions are absent from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds removal and preservation results.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets custom field selections, Lamha must remove exactly the selected fields from the exported copy while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a privacy export with selected custom fields, when the export runs, then only the selected fields are removed from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds exact-selection and preservation results.

st: When embedded-metadata removal targets all removable fields, Lamha must produce an export copy stripped of every removable field while preserving the original file.
ac: Given a full privacy export, when removal runs, then every removable embedded field is absent from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds full-strip and preservation results.

st: When face and AI privacy controls run, Lamha must let the user delete AI tags from the derived projections and rebuild them from versioned records without changing the original assets.
ac: Given stored AI tags, when deletion is confirmed, then the tags are removed from projections and rebuild restores them from versioned records.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds deletion and rebuild results.

st: When face and AI privacy controls run, Lamha must let the user delete embeddings from the derived projections and rebuild them from versioned records.
ac: Given stored embeddings, when deletion is confirmed, then the embeddings are removed and rebuild restores them from versioned records.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds deletion and rebuild results.

st: When the user requests entire-library AI data deletion, Lamha must delete all AI-derived projections and rebuild only from remaining versioned records.
ac: Given an entire-library deletion request, when it is confirmed, then all AI-derived projections are deleted and rebuild restores only what versioned records retain.
r: Privacy-scope label; rewrite adds whole-library deletion and rebuild results.

st: When the user requests AI data deletion for one asset, Lamha must delete that asset's AI-derived projections and rebuild them from versioned records without changing the asset file.
ac: Given one asset, when deletion is confirmed, then its AI projections are deleted and the asset file remains unchanged.
r: Privacy-scope label; rewrite adds scoped deletion and no-mutation.

st: When the user requests AI data deletion for one event, Lamha must delete that event's AI-derived projections and rebuild them from versioned records without changing media files.
ac: Given one event, when deletion is confirmed, then its AI projections are deleted and the event's media files remain unchanged.
r: Privacy-scope label; rewrite adds scoped deletion and no-mutation.

st: When face and AI privacy controls run, Lamha must let the user delete face boxes from the derived projections and rebuild them from versioned records.
ac: Given stored face boxes, when deletion is confirmed, then they are removed from projections and rebuild restores them from versioned records.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds deletion and rebuild results.

st: When face and AI privacy controls run, Lamha must let the user delete person assignments from the derived projections while keeping reviewed person records intact.
ac: Given stored assignments, when deletion is confirmed, then the assignments are removed from projections and person records remain intact.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds deletion and record preservation.

st: When face and AI privacy controls run, Lamha must let the user delete relationship links from the derived projections while keeping reviewed relationship records intact.
ac: Given stored relationship links, when deletion is confirmed, then the links are removed from projections and relationship records remain intact.
r: Privacy-field label; rewrite adds deletion and record preservation.

st: When the user requests AI data deletion for one person, Lamha must delete that person's AI-derived projections and rebuild them from versioned records without deleting the person profile.
ac: Given one person, when deletion is confirmed, then the person's AI projections are deleted and the profile remains intact.
r: Privacy-scope label; rewrite adds scoped deletion and profile preservation.

st: Autonomous cleanup must never delete code or data before a reviewed replacement is active; deletion requires replacement verification.
r: Autonomous-rule label; reclassified as a replacement-before-deletion constraint.
vm: Cleanup validation must fail on deletion without replacement.

st: When a trash operation would collide with an existing path, Lamha must warn before committing and require an explicit resolution.
ac: Given a trash collision, when the operation is prepared, then a warning is shown and nothing commits until resolution.
r: Trash label; rewrite adds warning and approval.

st: Every trash operation must record a typed operation record with source path, target path, and restore metadata.
ac: Given a trash operation, when it commits, then an operation record with source, target, and restore metadata is persisted.
r: Trash label; rewrite adds the operation record.

st: Trash must not purge automatically by default; purging requires an explicit user action and reviewed confirmation.
ac: Given a trashed asset, when no purge action is taken, then the asset remains in trash indefinitely.
r: Trash label; rewrite adds the no-auto-purge rule.

st: When an asset is trashed, Lamha must move the complete asset bundle (media, sidecars, and companions) together.
ac: Given an asset bundle, when trash commits, then every bundle member moves together.
r: Trash label; rewrite adds bundle cohesion.

st: When an asset is trashed, Lamha must preserve its event and tag references so restore returns the asset to the same organizational state.
ac: Given a trashed asset with event and tag references, when restore runs, then the references are intact.
r: Trash label; rewrite adds reference preservation.

st: Trash must preserve the original path of every trashed asset and restore must return it to that path.
ac: Given a trashed asset, when restore runs, then the asset returns to its original path.
r: Trash label; rewrite adds original-path preservation.

st: When a sidecar is missing externally, Lamha must mark the record degraded and open Review without fabricating values.

st: A partial hash match alone must never auto-relink an asset; ambiguous partial matches must open Review.

st: Capture date alone must not be used to relink externally changed assets; matching requires identity or full-hash evidence.

st: File size alone must not be used to relink externally changed assets; matching requires identity or full-hash evidence.
ac: Given a size match without identity evidence, when reconciliation runs, then no relink occurs.
r: External-change label; rewrite adds the size-only prohibition.

st: Sidecar references must be reconciled only when the referenced asset identity is confirmed; otherwise the sidecar stays unresolved in Review.

st: When new media appears on a connected external drive, Lamha must scan and index it under the same authorized-root rules.

st: External reconciliation must preserve the stable asset ID and must never assign a duplicate ID to a relinked asset.
ac: Given a relinked asset, when reconciliation runs, then the asset ID is preserved and no duplicate ID is created.

st: When an external delete is detected, Lamha must confirm the deletion with identity evidence and move the asset to trash or Review before removing any record.
ac: Given a detected external delete, when reconciliation runs, then the asset enters trash or Review and no record is removed without confirmation.

st: When a duplicate copy appears on an external drive, Lamha must create a reviewable duplicate candidate and must not delete or merge either file automatically.
ac: Given a duplicate copy, when detection runs, then a candidate is created and no file changes before confirmation.
r: External-change label; rewrite adds candidate creation and no-mutation.

st: When a new folder appears on an external drive, Lamha must index it under the root rules and must not treat it as authorized until reviewed.
ac: Given a new external folder, when scanning runs, then it is indexed under root rules and authorization is reviewed.
r: External-change label; rewrite adds indexing and authorization review.

st: When an external folder is renamed, Lamha must reconcile the path index on identity evidence and must not re-link assets on name alone.
ac: Given an externally renamed folder, when reconciliation runs, then the index updates with identity evidence and no asset relinks on name alone.
r: External-change label; rewrite adds identity-based reconciliation.

st: When an external drive disconnects, Lamha must switch that root to Detached Index Mode, keep records and pending overlays available, and mark affected operations deferred.

st: When an external drive reconnects, Lamha must reconcile the root manifest by durable drive identity and offer deterministic resume or rollback for deferred operations.

st: Timeline navigation must move through dates from local records, stay keyboard-operable, and preserve the prior position when loading fails.

st: The metadata panel must display the reviewed metadata fields from local records and remain readable and keyboard-accessible.

st: People browsing must render person profiles and faces from local records, stay keyboard-operable, and preserve the prior view when loading fails.

st: The target local architecture must retain the useful gallery components that render from local data and keep the gallery keyboard-operable.

st: Every UI-to-core call must use the reviewed typed Tauri IPC command and render returned local data; hard-coded production mock state is prohibited.
ac: Given a target screen, when it invokes the core, then the reviewed typed command is called and the visible result reflects returned local data.

st: The target local architecture must retain the useful metadata UI that reads and displays reviewed fields from local records.

r: Architecture label; rewrite names the retained behavior.

st: The Memories feature must provide a useful UI that derives each memory from local canonical asset references and omits unavailable assets without changing their records.

st: The target local architecture must retain the useful people UI that renders profiles, faces, and links from local records.

r: Architecture label; rewrite names the retained behavior.

st: The target local architecture must retain the useful search UI that returns matching local assets with source and revision information.

st: When external-drive behavior differs across platforms, Lamha must handle each difference with the reviewed drive rules and preserve records and overlays.

st: Mind-map loading must derive the map from canonical records within the reviewed performance budget and show a typed state when loading fails.

st: Duplicate processing must complete within the reviewed performance budget and must never delete or merge files automatically.

st: External-drive reconnect must reconcile within the reviewed performance budget and preserve records and pending overlays.

r: Performance label; rewrite adds budget and preservation.

ac: Given a rebuild workload, when SQLite is rebuilt, then it completes within budget and all saved decisions and revisions are restored.

st: Third-party licences must be inventoried with attribution and redistribution review and the release gate must fail while any licence is unresolved.

r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds presence and release blocking.

st: The release bundle must include the reviewed Immich attribution and the release gate must fail when it is missing.

r: Legal-surface label; rewrite adds presence and release blocking.

st: The release bundle must include the required copyright notices and the release gate must fail when any required notice is missing.

st: Metadata-library licences must be inventoried with attribution and redistribution review and the release gate must fail while any licence is unresolved.

st: Loose photo intake must add unassigned photos to Manage Later with reviewed metadata and no media movement until an approved plan.

st: Loose video intake must add unassigned videos to Manage Later with reviewed metadata and no media movement until an approved plan.

st: Existing-folder intake must link or adopt the selected existing folder without moving its contents and must index it in place.

r: Mapping-pass field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.

st: The current-architecture mapping must record the services used by each area and must reject rows without service evidence.
r: Mapping-pass field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Mapping validation must reject rows missing services.

r: Mapping-pass field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Mapping validation must reject rows missing repositories.

st: The current-architecture mapping must record ML requests made by each area and must reject rows without ML evidence.
r: Mapping-pass field label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
