st: Recursive scanning must traverse the Library Root tree, index supported media with stable identities, and stop at unauthorized boundaries.
ac: Given a Library Root, when recursive scanning runs, then supported media is indexed and traversal stops at unauthorized boundaries.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds traversal scope and boundary enforcement.

st: Incremental rescanning must process only changed or new paths and report the scanned scope without rescanning the whole library.
ac: Given an existing index, when incremental rescan runs, then only changed and new paths are processed and the scope is reported.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds scoped processing.

st: File watching must detect changes within the authorized root and reconcile the index without mutating source files.
ac: Given a watched root, when a file changes, then the index reconciles and the source file remains unchanged.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds change detection and no-mutation.

st: External change detection must reconcile the index with the current filesystem on the next scan and report mismatches without altering source files.
ac: Given external changes, when the next scan runs, then the index reconciles and mismatches are reported while source files remain unchanged.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds reconciliation and reporting.

st: Thumbnail generation must create previews from local media without modifying the originals and record generation state.
ac: Given an indexed asset, when thumbnail generation runs, then a preview is created from the local source and the original remains unchanged.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds preview creation and no-mutation.

st: Hash calculation must compute the full hash of each indexed file and store it with the asset record.
ac: Given an indexed file, when hash calculation runs, then the full hash is computed and stored with the record.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds hash computation and storage.

st: Sidecar discovery must find valid sidecars for each asset and link them without changing the sidecar bytes.
ac: Given an asset with sidecars, when discovery runs, then the sidecars are found and linked and their bytes remain unchanged.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds discovery and no-mutation.

st: Sidecar creation must write the reviewed schema-valid sidecar set through the transaction journal.
ac: Given an approved sidecar creation, when it commits, then the sidecar set is schema-valid and journaled.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds validity and journaling.

st: Sidecar health checks must report validity, missing fields, and degraded records without modifying the sidecars.
ac: Given sidecars, when health checks run, then validity and degraded state are reported and no sidecar changes occur.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds reporting and no-mutation.

st: Lamha must support read-only library roots by scanning and displaying them while keeping pending edits as overlays and never writing to the read-only media.
ac: Given a read-only root, when scanning and viewing run, then the library is available and edits are stored as overlays without writing to the root.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds read-only behavior.

st: When a configured Library Root is missing, Lamha must mark the root missing, keep its indexed records available, and defer operations until it returns.
ac: Given a missing root, when scanning runs, then the root is marked missing, records remain available, and operations are deferred.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds missing-root handling.

st: When a root reconnects, Lamha must reconcile it by durable identity and restore records and pending overlays.
ac: Given a reconnecting root, when reconciliation runs, then the root reconciles by identity and records and overlays are restored.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds identity reconciliation.

st: Selecting one or more library roots must record explicit user authorization and limit scans and writes to the authorized root set.
ac: Given selected roots, when selection is confirmed, then the roots are authorized and scans/writes are limited to them.
r: Scanning label; rewrite separates selection from authorization.

st: Existing folder recognition must identify previously indexed folders at their current paths and reconcile the index without moving them.
ac: Given an existing folder, when recognition runs, then it is identified and indexed in place without moving.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds in-place recognition.

st: Lamha must support external drives as Library Roots with durable drive identity, detached state, and reconnection reconciliation.
ac: Given an external drive, when it is used as a root, then scanning, detached state, and reconnection follow the reviewed drive rules.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds external-drive support.

st: Metadata extraction must read the reviewed fields from the media source and preserve the file bytes unchanged.
ac: Given a media file, when extraction runs, then the reviewed fields are read and the file remains unchanged.
r: Scanning label; rewrite adds extraction and preservation.

st: Lamha must keep support for the reviewed event types (trips, casual hangouts, one-day and multi-day events, and events with no known date).
ac: Given each reviewed event type, when event creation runs, then the type is supported with the reviewed rules.
r: Event label; rewrite names the supported set.

st: Trips must be supported as parent events that may contain optional child events.
ac: Given a trip, when event creation runs, then the trip is created as a parent event with optional children.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds parent semantics.

st: Casual hangouts must be supported as a lightweight event type with the reviewed naming and membership rules.
ac: Given a casual hangout, when event creation runs, then it is created with the reviewed rules.
r: Event-type label; rewrite names the type.

st: One-day events must be created with a single approved date and the reviewed folder naming.
ac: Given a one-day event, when it is created, then it uses the approved date and naming.
r: Event-type label; rewrite names the rule.

st: Multi-day events must be created with the approved start date and must not be split automatically.
ac: Given a multi-day event, when it is created, then it stays unified under the approved start date.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds unity.

st: Events continuing after midnight must remain unified under the approved start date and must not split on time alone.
ac: Given a midnight-spanning event, when it is created, then it remains unified under the approved start date.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds unity.

st: Events with no known date must use the Unknown Date layout and must not invent a calendar date.
ac: Given an event with no approved date, when it is created, then it uses Unknown Date and no date is invented.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds the no-date rule.

st: Events with multiple locations must store the reviewed location set and remain unified.
ac: Given an event with multiple locations, when it is created, then the location set is stored and the event remains unified.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds location-set storage.

st: Events with one primary folder must record the primary folder and use it as the materialization target.
ac: Given an event with one primary folder, when materialization runs, then the primary folder is used.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds primary-folder semantics.

st: Events linked to several folders must record the reviewed folder set and keep linked folders immobile.
ac: Given an event with several folders, when it is created, then the folder set is recorded and linked folders are not moved.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds folder-set and immobility.

st: Parent events must support child-event membership and preserve it in projections.
ac: Given a parent event, when child events are linked, then the membership persists and appears in projections.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds parent/child semantics.

st: Child events must record their parent membership and remain independently editable.
ac: Given a child event, when it is edited, then the parent membership persists and the child remains editable.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds child semantics.

st: Trips containing optional child events must allow optional membership and preserve it in projections.
ac: Given a trip, when optional child events are added, then the membership persists as optional.
r: Event-type label; rewrite adds optional-child semantics.

st: Event cover images must store the reviewed cover reference and display it in event views.
ac: Given an event, when a cover is chosen, then the reference is stored and displayed.
r: Event-field label; rewrite adds storage and display.

st: Event descriptions must store the reviewed description text and display it in event views.
ac: Given an event, when a description is saved, then it is stored and displayed.
r: Event-field label; rewrite adds storage and display.

st: Event tags must persist the reviewed namespaced tags and reflect them in tag projections.
ac: Given an event, when tags are saved, then the tags persist and appear in projections.
r: Event-field label; rewrite adds persistence and projection.

st: Event attendees must store the reviewed people set and reflect it in event and person projections.
ac: Given an event, when attendees are recorded, then the people set persists and appears in projections.
r: Event-field label; rewrite adds persistence and projection.

st: Event group presence must store the reviewed groups attending an event and reflect them in projections.
ac: Given an event, when group presence is recorded, then the groups persist and appear in projections.
r: Event-field label; rewrite adds persistence and projection.

st: Event relationship composition must derive from reviewed relationship rules and show its source.
ac: Given an event and reviewed relationships, when composition renders, then it derives from the rules with source shown.
r: Event-field label; rewrite adds derivation and source.

st: Physically merged folders must be represented as one managed folder with all member assets indexed in place.
ac: Given physically merged folders, when indexing runs, then they are represented as one folder with assets indexed in place.
r: Event-folder label; rewrite adds merged representation.

st: Logically linked folders must record the link without moving contents and must remain immobile.
ac: Given folders to link, when the link is confirmed, then the link is recorded and contents remain at their paths.
r: Event-folder label; rewrite adds link and immobility.

st: Split folders must preview the resulting folder set and commit only after approval while preserving asset identities.
ac: Given a folder split plan, when preview runs, then the resulting folders are shown and commit requires approval.
r: Event-folder label; rewrite adds preview and approval.

st: The existing-feature map must record the reviewed fields for each feature record and reject rows with missing fields.
r: Feature-map label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Feature-map validation must reject incomplete rows.

st: Manual event creation may display summaries such as date range, cameras, locations, file sizes, asset counts, existing folders, detected people, and known groups.
r: Manual-event heading; reclassified as glossary of optional summaries.

st: Date range is a summary field showing the reviewed capture-date range of the event's assets.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Cameras is a summary field listing the reviewed camera devices of the event's assets.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Locations is a summary field listing the reviewed locations of the event's assets.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: File sizes is a summary field showing the reviewed total size of the event's assets.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Selected asset count is a summary field showing the number of assets selected for the event.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Existing folders is a summary field showing the existing folders that may be linked to the event.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Detected people is a summary field showing the reviewed people detected in the event's assets.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Known groups is a summary field showing the reviewed groups among the event's people.
r: Summary-field label; reclassified as glossary.

st: Local albums must persist reviewed membership without duplicating media files.
ac: Given an album, when membership changes, then the membership persists and no media file is duplicated.
r: Album label; rewrite adds persistence and no-duplication.

st: Album covers must store the reviewed cover reference and display it in album views.
ac: Given an album, when a cover is chosen, then the reference is stored and displayed.
r: Album label; rewrite adds storage and display.

st: Album sorting must persist the reviewed sort rule and apply it to album views.
ac: Given an album, when sorting is changed, then the rule persists and views apply it.
r: Album label; rewrite adds persistence and application.

st: Albums must never cause physical duplication of media files; membership references the same asset identity.
ac: Given an asset in several albums, when albums render, then the same asset identity is referenced and no file is duplicated.
r: Album label; rewrite adds the no-duplication invariant.

st: One asset in several albums must reference the same asset identity in every album without duplication.
ac: Given an asset in several albums, when the asset is viewed, then every album references the same identity.
r: Album label; rewrite adds identity sharing.

st: Album metadata must persist the reviewed album fields in the authoritative record and display them in album views.
ac: Given an album, when metadata is saved, then the fields persist and display.
r: Album label; rewrite adds persistence and display.

st: Album filtering must return assets whose reviewed album membership matches the filter.
ac: Given album membership, when a filter is applied, then matching assets return.
r: Album label; rewrite adds the filter result.

st: The application must use the reviewed name Lamha consistently on every user-visible surface and the release gate must fail if any surface disagrees.
ac: Given the release build, when name validation runs, then every surface shows Lamha or release fails.
r: Rebranding label; rewrite adds consistency and release gating.

st: Favorite and unfavorite actions must persist the reviewed state and reflect it in the gallery.
ac: Given an asset, when favorite or unfavorite is used, then the state persists and the gallery reflects it.
r: Favorites label; rewrite adds persistence and reflection.

st: The dedicated Favorites view must show exactly the favorited assets from local data and remain keyboard-operable.
ac: Given favorited assets, when the Favorites view opens, then only favorited assets are shown from local data.
r: Favorites label; rewrite adds view scope.

st: Favorite state must be stored locally in the reviewed sidecar and must not depend on a server.
ac: Given a favorite change, when it is saved, then the state is stored in the local sidecar.
r: Favorites label; rewrite adds local storage.

st: When a search or smart view runs, Lamha must include favorite state as a filter from local records and return assets whose reviewed favorite state matches the filter.
ac: Given favorited assets, when a search or smart view runs, then favorite state filters results from local records and only matching assets return.
r: Favorites label; rewrite adds search, smart-view support, and filter results.
vm: Favorites search fixture with filter checks.

st: On this day memories must derive assets from local canonical records by date and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given local canonical assets, when On this day renders, then matching assets derive from records and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Same-month-in-previous-years memories must derive assets from local canonical records by month and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given local canonical assets, when the same-month view renders, then matching assets derive from records and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Location memories must derive assets from reviewed location records and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given location records, when location memories render, then matching assets derive from records and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Album memories must derive assets from reviewed album membership and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given album membership, when album memories render, then matching assets derive from membership and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Screenshot exclusions must exclude reviewed screenshot-class assets from memories.
ac: Given screenshot assets, when memories render, then excluded screenshots never appear.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds exclusion.

st: When memories are generated, Lamha must produce every memory entirely from local canonical records and must perform no upload or outbound network request.
ac: Given local canonical records, when memories are generated, then each memory is produced from local records and no upload or outbound request occurs.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds local-only generation and the no-upload result.

st: Event memories must derive assets from reviewed event membership and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given event membership, when event memories render, then matching assets derive from membership and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Folder and tag exclusions must exclude the reviewed folders and tags from memories.
ac: Given excluded folders and tags, when memories render, then matching assets never appear.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds exclusion.

st: The random continuous memory reel must derive assets from local canonical records, show a reproducible result, and omit unavailable assets without changing their records.
ac: Given local canonical assets, when the memory reel renders, then it derives from records, is reproducible, and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories-product label; rewrite keeps product meaning and adds reproducibility.

st: Person memories must derive assets from reviewed person assignments and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given person assignments, when person memories render, then matching assets derive from assignments and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Group memories must derive assets from reviewed group membership and omit unavailable assets.
ac: Given group membership, when group memories render, then matching assets derive from membership and unavailable assets are omitted.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds derivation.

st: Hidden-person exclusions must exclude assets whose only reviewed people are hidden from memories.
ac: Given hidden people, when memories render, then matching assets never appear.
r: Memories label; rewrite adds exclusion.

st: Pass 1 must map all meaningful code and exclusions and must not declare the map complete while exclusions remain.
ac: Given the codebase, when Pass 1 mapping runs, then every meaningful area and exclusion is recorded or the pass fails.
r: Planning-pass label; rewrite adds completeness and failure.

st: Pass 2 must map actual runtime and data flow and must not declare the map complete while flow evidence is missing.
ac: Given the codebase, when Pass 2 mapping runs, then runtime and data-flow evidence is recorded or the pass fails.
r: Planning-pass label; rewrite adds evidence and failure.

st: Pass 3 must map every user and technical capability and must not declare the map complete while any capability is unmapped.
ac: Given the codebase, when Pass 3 mapping runs, then every user and technical capability is mapped or the pass fails.
r: Planning-pass label; rewrite adds completeness and failure.

st: The Graphify pass must extract every requirement from the source plans and must fail when any requirement remains unextracted.
r: Graphify-pass label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Pass validation must fail on unextracted requirements.

st: The Graphify pass must map target modules for every requirement and must fail when any requirement lacks a target module.
r: Graphify-pass label; reclassified as a completeness constraint.
vm: Pass validation must fail on unmapped target modules.

st: Content suggestions from the local worker must carry model, source, and configuration provenance and remain reviewable until approved.
ac: Given a worker run, when content suggestions are produced, then they carry provenance and remain unapplied until approval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds provenance and approval gate.

st: The hardware benchmark must measure the local worker's CPU, RAM, GPU memory, and latency on the declared hardware and record results with the hardware profile.
ac: Given declared hardware, when the benchmark runs, then all required metrics are recorded with the hardware profile.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds measurable metrics and recording.

st: The local worker must select CPU, GPU, or hybrid execution from the reviewed hardware assessment and record the selected provider with each task.
ac: Given assessed hardware, when a task runs, then the provider is selected from the assessment and recorded with the task.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds provider selection and recording.

st: Metadata mutation snapshots must be versioned and must restore the exact prior values on rollback.
ac: Given a versioned snapshot, when rollback runs, then the exact prior values are restored.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds versioning and restore.

st: Batch metadata operations must preview the full change set and commit only after approval while reporting per-item results.
ac: Given a batch operation, when preview runs, then the change set is shown and commit requires approval with per-item results.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds preview, approval, and reporting.

st: Unmanage Asset must remove the asset from managed organization while preserving the media file and its authority records.
ac: Given an asset, when Unmanage Asset is confirmed, then the asset leaves managed organization and the media file and records remain intact.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds preservation.

st: Privacy export must produce copies stripped of the reviewed private fields while leaving the original media unchanged.
ac: Given a privacy export, when it runs, then the copies omit private fields and the original remains unchanged.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds omission and preservation.

st: Clear app metadata must remove the reviewed app-owned metadata from assets while preserving media bytes and authority records.
ac: Given an asset, when app metadata is cleared, then the reviewed fields are removed and media bytes remain unchanged.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds removal and preservation.

st: Embedded metadata removal must strip the selected embedded fields from exported copies while preserving the original file.
ac: Given an export with selected fields, when removal runs, then the fields are stripped from the copy and the original remains unchanged.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds stripping and preservation.

st: Reconnection must reconcile the external drive by durable identity and restore records and pending overlays.
ac: Given a reconnecting drive, when reconciliation runs, then the drive reconciles by identity and records and overlays are restored.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds identity reconciliation.

st: External moves must update the path index on identity or full-hash evidence and must never auto-match on filename or partial hash.
ac: Given an external move, when reconciliation runs, then the index updates on identity evidence and ambiguous cases open Review.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds the identity rule.

st: External renames must update the path index on identity or full-hash evidence and must never auto-match on name alone.
ac: Given an external rename, when reconciliation runs, then the index updates on identity evidence and ambiguous cases open Review.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds the identity rule.

st: Sidecar recovery must restore the last validated sidecar state from journaled backups without guessing fields.
ac: Given a damaged sidecar, when recovery runs, then the last validated state is restored and no field is guessed.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds recovery and no-guessing.

st: Detached Index Mode must keep indexed records and pending overlays available for a disconnected drive and defer structural operations.
ac: Given a disconnected drive, when Detached Index Mode is active, then records and overlays remain available and operations are deferred.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds detached-mode behavior.

st: Drive identity must be a durable identifier recorded at registration and used for all reconnection and detached-state reconciliation.
ac: Given a registered drive, when it reconnects, then the durable identity matches and reconciliation uses it.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds durable identity.

st: Cross-drive operations must use copy, flush, checksum verification, and journaled source removal and must never assume atomic rename.
ac: Given a cross-drive operation, when it runs, then copy, flush, checksum, and journaled removal complete or the prior state is restored.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds the non-atomic rule.

st: Crash recovery must reconcile uncommitted manifests by transaction UUID and auto-finalize or roll back only when deterministic.
ac: Given an uncommitted manifest, when recovery runs, then deterministic cases finalize or roll back and non-deterministic cases open Review.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds determinism boundary.

st: AI cache rebuild must regenerate the rebuildable AI projections from versioned records without losing user decisions.
ac: Given versioned AI records, when the cache is rebuilt, then projections regenerate and user decisions remain intact.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds regeneration and preservation.

st: Sidecar verification must validate every sidecar against its schema and report degraded records without modifying them.
ac: Given sidecars, when verification runs, then validity is checked and degraded records are reported without modification.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds validation and no-mutation.

st: Global backup must inventory every authoritative record and media file in the backup manifest and verify the backup set.
ac: Given a backup run, when it completes, then the manifest inventories all records and files and the set verifies.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds inventory and verification.

st: Index rebuild must regenerate SQLite and caches from authoritative records and preserve every saved decision.
ac: Given authority records, when the index is rebuilt, then projections regenerate and saved decisions remain intact.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds regeneration and preservation.

st: Event backups must include event records, membership, folders, and sidecars and verify the backup set.
ac: Given an event backup, when it completes, then all event data is included and the set verifies.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds completeness and verification.

st: Large-library optimization must define and measure performance budgets (scan, index, search, thumbnail, and UI responsiveness at declared asset counts) and must block release when any budget is exceeded; it is not a storage-root authorization operation.
ac: Given each declared large-library workload, when the benchmark runs, then every required metric is measured against its budget and any exceedance blocks release.
r: Mandatory correction: the label was routed through the root-authorization template; rewrite restores measurable performance budgets.

st: Thumbnail scheduling must prioritize visible thumbnails and complete generation within the reviewed budget without blocking the UI.
ac: Given a gallery workload, when thumbnail scheduling runs, then visible thumbnails are prioritized and the UI remains responsive.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds scheduling and responsiveness.

st: Graph virtualization must render only the visible nodes and edges within the reviewed budget and keep navigation responsive.
ac: Given a large graph, when virtualization renders, then only visible nodes and edges render and navigation stays responsive.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds virtualization and responsiveness.

st: Background-job UX must expose typed progress and recovery state and must never report success for a failed or cancelled job.
ac: Given a background job, when it progresses or fails, then typed state is exposed and no false success is reported.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds typed state and no-false-success.

st: Memory usage must be measured and recorded against the reviewed budget for every declared workload and any exceedance must block release; memory here means RAM consumption, not the Memories product feature.
ac: Given each declared workload, when memory measurement runs, then RAM usage is recorded against the budget and exceedance blocks release.
r: Mandatory correction: label means RAM in the performance phase; rewrite separates the resource metric from the Memories feature.

st: Accessibility must provide keyboard, focus, semantic, screen-reader, and non-visual alternatives for every reviewed surface.
ac: Given each reviewed surface, when accessibility checks run, then every supported action is reachable by keyboard and assistive technology.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds equivalence and testability.

st: Bundled AI components must have pinned versions, licence and provenance records, and packaging evidence before release.
ac: Given each bundled AI component, when packaging validation runs, then version, licence, and provenance are recorded or release fails.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds packaging evidence and release blocking.

st: Bundled media tools must have pinned versions, licence records, and packaging evidence before release.
r: Phase label; reclassified as a packaging constraint.
vm: Packaging validation must require tool records.

st: Signing paths must be recorded per platform and signing must fail the release gate when any path or certificate is unresolved.
ac: Given the release manifest, when signing validation runs, then every signing path is recorded and unresolved entries block release.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds recording and release blocking.

st: Phase 2 must introduce the reviewed Lamha internal identity (name, identifiers, and branding surfaces) without removing required legal material.
ac: Given the rebranding plan, when identity is introduced, then the reviewed surfaces update and legal material remains intact.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds identity scope and legal preservation.

st: Rebranding must preserve legal notices and the release gate must fail if any required notice is removed.
ac: Given the pre-release surface set, when rebranding completes, then every required legal notice remains or release fails.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds notice preservation.

st: The desktop shell must establish the reviewed Tauri 2 process, typed IPC boundary, and permission model before other shell features.
ac: Given the shell bootstrap, when Tauri 2 is established, then the process, typed boundary, and permissions are in place.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds the shell foundation.

st: The scanner must index media within authorized roots, preserve source bytes, and report typed errors for unsupported or unreadable files.
ac: Given an authorized root, when the scanner runs, then supported media is indexed and unsupported or unreadable files return typed errors.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds scan behavior and errors.

st: The watcher must detect changes within authorized roots and reconcile the index without modifying source files.
ac: Given a watched root, when a change occurs, then the index reconciles and the source file remains unchanged.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds change detection and no-mutation.

st: Asset bundles must keep media and companion sidecars together for moves, renames, trash, and restore.
ac: Given an asset bundle, when any bundle operation runs, then all members move together.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds bundle cohesion.

st: The Authorized Path Set must limit scans and writes and reject any path outside the set before filesystem access.
ac: Given authorized and unauthorized paths, when access is requested, then only authorized paths pass and others return typed errors before I/O.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds pre-I/O rejection.

st: The XMP adapter must read and write the reviewed XMP fields and keep them aligned with the authoritative JSON record.
ac: Given an asset, when the XMP adapter runs, then the reviewed fields are valid and aligned with JSON.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds validity and alignment.

st: The timeline must render from local records, stay keyboard-operable, and preserve the prior position when loading fails.
ac: Given a local timeline, when it renders, then items come from local records and a failed load preserves the prior position.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds local rendering and stability.

st: Asset details must display the reviewed record fields from local data and remain accessible.
ac: Given an asset, when details open, then reviewed fields display from local data.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds display and accessibility.

st: Link must record a reviewed event or folder link without moving contents.
ac: Given a link action, when it is confirmed, then the link is recorded and contents remain at their paths.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds link and no-mutation.

st: Split must preview the resulting events or folders and commit only after approval while preserving membership history.
ac: Given a split plan, when preview runs, then the resulting set is shown and commit requires approval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds preview and approval.

st: Manage Later must keep unreviewed assets in a reviewed intake state without moving media until an approved plan.
ac: Given unreviewed assets, when Manage Later runs, then they stay in intake state and no media moves until approval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds intake state and plan gating.

st: The event schema must define the reviewed event fields and validation must reject records missing required fields.
ac: Given the event schema, when an event is written, then missing required fields are rejected.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds schema validation.

st: The manual event builder must create events from reviewed inputs with preview and approval before materialization.
ac: Given manual inputs, when the builder runs, then the event is previewed and materialization requires approval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds preview and approval.

st: Event JSON/XMP must persist the reviewed event fields and keep both representations aligned.
ac: Given an event, when JSON/XMP is written, then the fields are valid and aligned.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds validity and alignment.

st: Folder normalization must apply the reviewed naming rules with preview and approval while preserving original names.
ac: Given a folder name, when normalization is proposed, then the safe name is previewed and applied only after approval with the original preserved.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds preview, approval, and preservation.

st: Linked folders must remain immobile and automated organization must never move or rename them.
ac: Given a linked folder, when organization runs, then its paths and contents remain unchanged.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds immobility.

st: Face clusters must be reviewable and merges or splits must persist provenance and allow undo.
ac: Given face clusters, when a merge or split is confirmed, then the change persists with provenance and undo restores the prior state.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds reviewability and undo.

st: Person and group naming must preserve the stable ID and retain old names as searchable aliases.
ac: Given a rename, when it is confirmed, then the ID is unchanged and old names remain searchable.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds identity and alias preservation.

st: Hide must remove a person or group from default lists without deleting the profile or links.
ac: Given a hidden person or group, when lists render, then the profile and links remain and the item is excluded.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds exclusion and preservation.

st: When a person's or group's membership changes, Lamha must append or close the effective-dated period and keep every historical membership period queryable with its original interval.
ac: Given a membership change, when history is queried, then every prior period remains queryable with its original interval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds period semantics and history preservation.

st: When a user adds a subgroup to a group, Lamha must persist the reviewed hierarchical membership and reflect the subgroup in group and person projections.
ac: Given a group, when a subgroup is added, then the hierarchy persists and appears in group and person projections.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds subgroup semantics and projection.

st: Suppression must persist the reviewed suppression and exclude matching future proposals from review queues.
ac: Given a suppression, when it is confirmed, then it persists and matching future proposals are excluded.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds persistence and exclusion.

st: Tag namespaces must persist the reviewed namespace with each tag and validation must reject unnamespaced tags.
ac: Given a tag, when it is written, then its namespace is persisted and unnamespaced tags are rejected.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds namespace enforcement.

st: Tag activation must be review-first and AI-suggested tags must remain unapplied until approved.
ac: Given a suggested tag, when activation is requested, then the tag stays a candidate until approval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds the review-first rule.

st: Importer attribution must be stored independently and never inferred from photographer or camera-owner roles.
ac: Given an imported asset, when attribution is recorded, then the importer is stored separately from other roles.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds role independence.

st: Attribution changes must record provenance and revision and never silently change another role.
ac: Given an attribution change, when it is saved, then provenance and revision are recorded and other roles remain unchanged.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds provenance and independence.

st: Mind-map drafts must be saved safely and restored from the last valid state on failure.
ac: Given a draft, when it is saved, then the draft persists and a failed write leaves the last valid state recoverable.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds safe save and restore.

st: Mind-map materialization must preview nodes, edges, and filesystem effects and commit only after approval.
ac: Given a mind map, when materialization is requested, then the effects are previewed and commit requires approval.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds preview and approval.

st: The folder/event map must derive from canonical folder and event records and show its source.
ac: Given canonical records, when the folder/event map renders, then it derives from the records with source shown.
r: Phase label; rewrite adds derivation and source.

st: Event context links must navigate to the reviewed event context without changing records.
ac: Given an event context link, when it is opened, then the context loads and no record changes.
r: Phase label; rewrite separates navigation from mutation.

st: Suppression rules must persist the reviewed rule and exclude matching future proposals from review queues.
ac: Given a suppression rule, when it is confirmed, then it persists and matching future proposals are excluded.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds persistence and exclusion.

st: OCR indexes must be rebuildable from versioned OCR records and search must report stale or unavailable index data.
ac: Given versioned OCR records, when the index is rebuilt, then search returns results with provenance and stale data is reported.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds rebuildability and stale reporting.

st: Maps must render from canonical location records and show source and confidence where applicable.
ac: Given canonical location records, when a map renders, then results derive from the records with source shown.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds derivation and source.

st: Settings changes must validate and persist the local setting with a new revision and retain the previous value on failure.
ac: Given a settings change, when it is saved, then the effective value updates with a revision and failure retains the previous value.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds validation, persistence, and failure retention.

st: When a reviewer records a decision on a Review item, Lamha must persist the chosen value with its provenance and the review revision, and the recorded decision must remain visible in the item's history.
ac: Given a Review item, when a decision is recorded, then the chosen value, provenance, and review revision persist and remain visible in the item's history.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds persistence, provenance, and visible history.

st: Asset JSON must be read and written as the schema-valid authoritative record with exact-byte preservation on validation failure.
ac: Given an asset, when its JSON is read or written, then the record is schema-valid and malformed content is preserved.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds validity and preservation.

st: Library roots must be user-authorized and scans and writes must be limited to the authorized root set.
ac: Given an authorized root, when scans or writes run, then they stay within the authorized set.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds authorization enforcement.
Statement is already record-specific (XMP mirror read/write preserves exact bytes and keeps authority alignment); no legacy template is reproduced.

st: SQLite must remain a rebuildable index and must never be the only copy of user knowledge.
ac: Given authoritative records, when SQLite is rebuilt, then user knowledge is restored from the records.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds rebuildability.

st: People records must persist stable identities, names, faces, and links and preserve them across changes.
ac: Given a person record, when any field changes, then the stable identity and other fields remain intact.
r: Originals label; rewrite adds identity and field preservation.
